newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee stays weak by close, may sag again.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee stays weak by close, may sag again.

text.p: London coffee futures ended Friday lower by almost one-third on the week. But traders said roaster price-fixations at the lows and lack of fresh sales in the afternoon helped some positions to finish above the day's floor.
"There were some left-over orders after the long liquidation rise on the close yesterday," said one. "But there was no much left to be sold today."

Traders cited no fresh fundamental news but said sentiment was hurt by this week's news of Colombia allowing unrestricted coffee registrations for July and August and forecasts of a frost-free weekend in Brazil's coffee areas.
"Based on weather forecasts, there is no danger of the first white weekend in Brazil," said one trader.
News Brazil was asking coffee exporters to make no further sales for June came after the London market had closed and had no impact.

London's July robusta finished 4.2 percent or $80 down on the day at $1,825 a tonne after hitting a low at $1,815 and well below its previous support at $1,835. Prices gapped just $45 lower basis July, well above earlier expecations of $110 down.

In all, the market had lost some 32 percent in a week alone as it took a sharp downward swing from a rally that had taken London prices to 20-month highs in late May, and propelled New York arabicas to the strongest in 20 years.
Traders said Thursday's slide on sell-stops, which eroded values by some 8.5 percent, was further exaggerated by long liquidation by day-traders.

Last week's breakthrough to $2,670, the 20-month-peak basis July, was also fuelled by aggressive industry price-fixing. But roasters had since stood aside, awaiting to see further falls before committing themselves.
Volume reached 9,141 lots. July-Sept switch was traded at $25-$30 and Sept/Nov at $10-12.
Traders said it was still early to tell if the rally since early January had come to an end.
But they noted that there was a vacuum between Friday's level and the next key support area at $1,680.
"I don't think the market is really close to the bottom yet," said one trader.

Technical analysts said the rally over the last few weeks had been overdone and the market was now staging a downward correction which was long overdue. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
